eras.name: Early networks
eras.background: Networks that learn their weights from examples date back to the perceptron, and backpropagation made multi-layer networks trainable. With little data and compute they won only narrow tasks such as reading digits, and other methods dominated.

eras.name: Deep learning
eras.text: GPUs, big data and deeper nets
eras.background: Large labeled datasets and GPUs made far bigger networks trainable. A string of fixes for initialization, normalization and depth let networks grow deep, and they overtook hand-built features in vision and speech.

eras.name: Attention and diffusion
eras.text: New architectures for sequences and images
eras.background: Attention replaced recurrence as the way to model sequences, and one architecture came to serve language, vision and audio. In generation, diffusion replaced GANs as the way to produce images.

nodes.label: Perceptron
nodes.problem: Pattern recognition relied on hand-written rules.
nodes.idea: A single artificial neuron learns its weights from labeled examples.
nodes.impact: One layer cannot learn even XOR, and interest in neural networks faded.

nodes.label: Backprop
nodes.idea: Send error gradients backward through the layers with the chain rule.
nodes.impact: Revived neural networks, and it is still how every network is trained.

from.why: One layer could not learn even XOR, and multi-layer networks had no practical training method.

nodes.label: LSTM
nodes.idea: Gated memory cells keep the error signal alive across many steps.
nodes.impact: Ran speech recognition and translation until Transformers arrived.

from.why: Backpropagated through time, gradients vanish over long sequences, so recurrent networks forget.

nodes.label: LeNet-5
nodes.idea: Convolution and pooling layers learn features from pixels, trained end to end.
nodes.impact: Read bank checks commercially and became the template for later CNNs.

from.why: Backprop could train convolution filters in place of hand-designed features.

nodes.label: AlexNet
nodes.idea: Train a large CNN on GPUs with ReLU and dropout on ImageNet.
nodes.impact: Won ImageNet by a wide margin and started the deep learning boom.

from.why: CNNs worked on digits but were too slow to train on large image datasets.

nodes.label: VAE
nodes.problem: Deep latent-variable models were hard to train.
nodes.idea: The reparameterization trick lets gradients flow through random sampling.
nodes.impact: Made deep generative models trainable; VAEs later compress images for diffusion.

nodes.label: GAN
nodes.problem: Generative models needed probabilities that were intractable to compute.
nodes.idea: Train a generator to fool a discriminator that tells real from fake.
nodes.impact: Produced the sharpest generated images for years, though training was unstable.

nodes.label: Batch norm
nodes.idea: Normalize each layer's inputs over the mini-batch.
nodes.impact: Faster, more stable training; normalization layers became standard.

from.why: Deep networks trained slowly and needed careful initialization.

nodes.label: ResNet
nodes.idea: Skip connections let each block learn only a residual.
nodes.impact: Networks went far deeper, and residual connections are now in almost every model.

from.why: Stacking more layers made plain networks train worse, not better.
Supplied the normalization that keeps each residual block stable.

nodes.label: Transformer
nodes.idea: Self-attention relates all positions at once, in parallel.
nodes.impact: Became the architecture of LLMs and much of vision.

from.why: Recurrent models process tokens one at a time, which is slow to train on large data.

nodes.label: DDPM
nodes.idea: Learn to reverse a gradual noising process, one small step at a time.
nodes.impact: Diffusion overtook GANs and now powers image and video generation.

from.why: Its samples were blurry, but its variational training objective carried over to diffusion.
GANs made sharp images but were unstable to train and could miss whole kinds of images.

main.title: CMU 11-785: Introduction to Deep Learning
main.why: Backpropagation and optimization, CNNs, RNNs and LSTMs, attention and Transformers, then VAEs, diffusion and GANs. In English.

main.title: Learning Representations by Back-propagating Errors
main.why: Perceptrons could not learn hidden features, so backpropagation sends error gradients back through the layers to train them.

main.title: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Deep Feedforward Neural Networks
main.why: Deep nets trained poorly because activations and gradients shrank layer by layer, so Xavier initialization scales weights to keep their variance steady.

further.title: Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification

main.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
main.why: Large networks overfit, so dropout randomly removes units during training, like averaging many thinned networks.

main.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
main.why: One global learning rate fits parameters poorly, so Adam adapts each parameter's step from running averages of its gradients.

main.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
main.why: Shifting layer input distributions slow training, so batch normalization normalizes them over each mini-batch.

main.title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
main.why: Nets fit random labels, so classic theory cannot explain why they generalize.

further.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt

main.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
main.why: Hand-designed features limited recognition, so LeNet-5 learns convolution and pooling layers end to end from pixels.

main.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
main.why: AlexNet trained a large CNN on GPUs with ReLU and dropout, won the ImageNet challenge and started the deep learning boom.

further.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
further.why: VGG stacks many small convolutions instead of large filters and shows that depth alone buys accuracy.

main.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
main.why: Deeper plain networks trained worse, so ResNet adds skip connections that let layers learn residuals.

main.title: Long Short-Term Memory
main.why: RNN gradients vanish over long sequences, so LSTM adds gated memory cells that keep the error signal alive.
Recurrent models process tokens one at a time, so the Transformer replaces recurrence with self-attention that trains in parallel.

main.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
main.why: Latent-variable models were hard to train, so the VAE uses the reparameterization trick to train them by gradient descent.

main.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
main.why: Instead of modeling densities directly, a GAN trains a generator to fool a discriminator.

main.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
main.why: DDPM learns to reverse a gradual noising process and generates images by removing noise step by step.

main.title: Applying Deep Learning to Airbnb Search
main.why: Gradient boosted trees plateaued for Airbnb's search ranking, so it moved to neural networks and shares what failed along the way.
LinkedIn's feed used one logistic regression per objective, which it replaced with one multi-task network in TensorFlow.
Uber corrects routing-engine ETAs with a learned model, which moved from XGBoost to a low-latency linear transformer.
Shopify's product categorizer read only English text, so it moved to pretrained image and multilingual text embeddings feeding chained heads, one per taxonomy level.
